svg.aria-label: Research frontier. Q.01: Regression, or noise? An agent changes: a prompt edit, a model version, a tool schema, a refactored loop. Its outputs are stochastic and multi-turn, so one run proves nothing either way. Which differences are real, and which layer caused them? Working answer: pass^k sampling, McNemar's exact test as a merge gate, trajectory diffs to locate the change. Q.02: When is a judge allowed to judge? LLM-as-judge is cheap and scales, but a lenient judge quietly lets regressions through. How much agreement with human labels is enough before a judge may block a merge, and which deterministic checks must sit underneath it? Working answer: calibrate against a golden set (κ, FPR, FNR), back the judge with rule assertions. Q.03: What does an adapter actually learn? LoRA trains a low-rank update on a frozen model. Separating a genuine domain gain from memorised formatting needs base and adapter evaluated on the same held-out examples, with provenance for both. Working answer: base-versus-adapter evaluation on held-out data, verified artifacts only. Q.04: Can structure define a unit of work? Time and line counts are weak proxies for "this feature is done". Can syntax-tree changes, weighted by depth, spread and confidence, recognise a meaningful milestone without asking the developer? Working answer: weighted milestone scoring over AST diffs.
